name: Italian medieval spectacles
description: A 1306 Florentine sermon discussed eyeglasses as a means to improve vision.

impact.note: A sermon dates the arrival of spectacles, read as a capability, which restored working sight widely and fed the lens craft behind later optical instruments.

date.basis: Date applies to this specific event or witness, not global invention.

events.statement: A 1306 Florentine sermon discussed eyeglasses as a means to improve vision.

evidence.locator: Transparent Glass in the West, pp. 136–137
evidence.supports: Dillon discusses Giordano da Pisa’s 1306 sermon mentioning vision aids. It is a textual witness, not an identified inventor or definite invention date.

events.caveats: The text is a later-recorded sermon, not a surviving dated pair or proof that its author was the inventor. Exact origin and dating remain debated.
